prompt: Precision-assembly visual action benchmark. One 320x320 RGB scene showing a steel ring (inner edges around its central bore) and the stationary round peg below. Move the HOLE part horizontally so its aperture center is exactly above the stationary peg axis. Ignore the handle. Predict the ideal move in robot world millimeters. Camera looks downward, tilted 20.0 degrees toward world +Y. Image right = +X, up = away toward +Y. FOV 30 degrees vertical, optical center (159.5,159.5). Nominal camera working distance roughly 360 mm. Nominal aperture width 62.35 mm. Peg width or diameter 60.35 mm. Account for parallax and any occlusion. Use only this image and prompt. No tools. Output only one JSON object with dx and dy in mm, to one decimal place. Also align the moving hole plane parallel to the table using rotation about world X (roll) and, for square peg only, around world Z (yaw). Initially the part may be aligned already. Handle points along +X at zero yaw. Positive roll raises +Y side; positive yaw rotates +X toward +Y. Give angular CORRECTIONS in degrees about the aperture center (apply as increments to current world roll and yaw). Return only JSON with four numeric keys dx, dy, roll, yaw. Use yaw=0 for a cylindrical peg.
